messages.author: 07c144b7018cfe97
messages.subject: ocurrence() error
parts:
Dear all

I am trying to use the function occurrence(). However, I obtain an error that I am not able to understand: "Error in if (CTMM$error) { : argument is of length zero"

I suspected that this means that one of my individuals has not enough positions. However, when I run akde() function I have not similar problems.

I attach my script just in case could be useful 

Thanks in advances!

Eneko

df<-as.data.frame(MYDATA)

#1
TL<-as.telemetry(df, timesformat="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", timezone = "UTC")

#2
TL <- lapply(TL,
             function(x) x[round(seq(1,
                                     nrow(x),
                                     length.out = 100),
                                 0),])

#3
GUESS <- lapply(TL,
                function(x) ctmm.guess(x,
                                       interactive=FALSE))

#4
FITS <- lapply(1:length(TL),
               function(i) ctmm.fit(TL[[i]],
                                    GUESS[[i]])
)

#5
names(FITS) <- names(TL)

#6
UDS <- akde(TL,
            FITS,
            weights = TRUE)

#7
BB<-occurrence(TL,FITS)

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: ocurrence() error
parts:
Hi Eneko,

I have not yet coded occurrence() to output aligned UDs from list arguments like I have for akde(), so for now you would have to do something like

BB <- lapply(1:length(TL),function(i) occurrence(TL[[i]],FITS[[i]]) )

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: ocurrence() error
parts:
Thanks you a lot Chris

Now the lapply() for occurrence() works. However, it is very fast (which results strange for me) and if I try to plot the results with: 

plot(TL,UD=BB[1])

Which works when I use to akde() results, give me the next error:

Error in `.rowNamesDF<-`(x, value = value) : invalid 'row.names' length

Also, if I try to generate the polygons for export it as shp as I make with akde() results, 

Poligono.95<-lapply(1:length(BB),
                    function(i) SpatialPolygonsDataFrame.UD(BB[[i]],level.UD=0.95,level=0.95))

occurs a fatal error and R sesion is aborted.



I addition I would like to make you a final question. I am dealing with the gaps in my data. I understand perfectly how dt.max argument of occurrence() works. However, it is difficult to me understand how works argument cor.min

Thank you a lot


Cheers


Eneko

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: ocurrence() error
parts:
Hi Eneko,

If you can message/email me a minimal working example (data and script) to reproduce the issue, then I can take a look at it. occurrence() should be slower than akde().

In current versions of the package (on GitHub) cor.min maintains the specified fraction of velocity correlation over the gap, meaning that within the gap the motion is relatively ballistic and gaps are no longer filled in when they are so wide that there is little knowledge of where the individual is going within.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: ocurrence() error
parts:
Hi Eneko,

If your subsampling was so coarse that it made the data IID, then I think the current code would just pop out the empirical distribution, which would be fast. You can't interpolate between IID data. If that's not the case, then I can take a look if you send me a minimal working example.

Best,
Chris
